section_reviews.checked: Definitions distinguish tongue position, rounding, vowel quantity and weight. Reconstruction stars, historical arrows and coexisting paradigm forms remain separate. No new IPA or obligatory production task is introduced.
source_basis: Fulk §§62, 74, 109, 132; source-printed reconstructions checked at their individual locators

section_reviews.checked: dæg/dagas and cræftum correctly distinguish open-syllable restoration from a closed syllable. Immediate w is a separate condition. The stressed-root scope is explicit without saying that brightening never affected unstressed vowels.

Immediate inputs æ/e/i; stress restriction; rj exclusion and rr inclusion; vowel-specific l-cluster limits; *hælp/healp versus helpan; short ea in healp/eald; separate long-vowel breaking; subsequent West Saxon io/eo merger. The table does not claim all diphthongs or all front vowels behave alike.
source_basis: Fulk Appendix A IV.28 p.111/PDF123 and V.45 p.113/PDF125

section_reviews.checked: Selected mutation correspondences preserve length and limit nasal history. fēt is correctly identified in both selected uses. dōm/dēman is a word-family comparison and *dōm(i)jan is Fulk’s printed reconstruction. eald/ieldra/ieldest reflects successive processes. hǣtt is allowed by Cook hǣt(t). helpan/hilpð and ēo/īe are not falsely made one later umlaut event. Final revision correctly identifies loss of the conditioning sound, not the entire surviving ending.

Palatal diphthongization follows breaking and has distinct consonant-to-vowel direction and West Saxon scope. geaf/gēafon retain different quantities. Back mutation gives the relevant vowel and single-labial/liquid limits, including the special effect of following a. heofon/hefon is transparently a new teaching comparison of separately printed source forms. Late West Saxon and Anglian smoothing have separate labels and conditions; hēh has visible headword access.
source_basis: Fulk Appendix B I.3 p.118/PDF130; I.5 and III.12 p.119/PDF131

section_reviews.checked: cēlan/*kōljan illustrates chronology without replacing the pronunciation guide with an exceptionless written-vowel rule. j-gemination has light-syllable scope and the r exception; the added §7 pointer supports that term. Gothic bidjan is labelled a cognate, never an ancestor or an Old English form.
source_basis: Cook §§33–36 pp.24–25/PDF40–41 and Appendix V p.268/PDF284

section_reviews.checked: Ordinary noun stem-weight comparison is bounded; word has short o but is heavy, while wīf is heavy through ī. High-vowel loss is not generalized to all endings. hēafodes is a full-stem analogical variant rather than an unexplained exception. *seohan/sēon and seoh preserve the contrast in quantity and h environment; contraction and compensatory lengthening are distinguished.

drīfan and helpan principal parts are coexisting forms. The account separates inherited ablaut from breaking and present raising. cweðan/cweden is a supported comparison; Verner’s law is early accent-conditioned voicing, preceding ordinary Germanic stress, with subsequent developments. Ordinary Old English contextual fricative voicing is not confused with the inherited alternation. Analogy is bounded by recorded paradigms.

Summary retains preceding qualifications. All thirteen note families identify actual source sections and printed/one-based PDF pages. Cook’s æ correction, older e raising, Fulk’s finer breaking conditions, omission of palatal dots, separate Gothic status and source-context correction are explicitly identified.

findings.issue: The initial definitions of brightening, breaking, palatal diphthongization and back mutation did not locate the teaching account in stressed roots; breaking in particular could be misapplied to unstressed endings.
findings.requested_change: State the stressed-vowel scope locally or through a clear governing statement, retaining vowel-specific and dialect limits.
findings.resolution: SH-AUTH-REV01 adds local qualifiers, the short stressed-vowel table header, corresponding summary wording and the exact Fulk V.45 source note. Actual revised passages were reread.
findings.important_limit_on_resolution: This is not a claim that every named process operated only under stress. Fulk Appendix A IV.26 and IV.30 explicitly also describe brightening and front mutation in unstressed syllables. The master scopes its chosen examples without asserting exclusivity. Only breaking is explicitly excluded from unstressed syllables by Fulk V.45.
